findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed no barrier to be used by staff when hand washing. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were properly rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used when handling handwashing faucet to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed cheese to be cold holding at 55F. Discussed with PIC, cheese was placed in the back right corner of prep cooler directly next to hot holding. A lid was brought to cheese and was moved to a different location is prep cooler, cheese then tested at 41F. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed no thermometer to be present within walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, thermometer was brought to walk in cooler. Ensure all coolers have a thermometer available.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed top of microwave and hot holding trays to have an accumulation of food debris present. Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents any buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed shelving unit across from triple sink to be significantly rusted. Discussed with PIC, shelving unit will be replaced. Ensure staff is monitoring/replacing facility equipment as needed
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair in the following areas:
1) The back triple sink caulking was observed to have black mold present.
2) The caulking at the back hand sink was observed coming apart from wall. Reseal. 

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed multiple boxes to be resting under a leaking Walk in Freezer unit. Discussed with PIC, a pan was placed on top of boxes to act as a barrier to the leak. Ensure food is protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, and holding of food. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the back metal panel of hood system to have an accumulation of grease below the baffles. Discussed with PIC. Ensure hood system is being cleaned at a frequency that prevents grease accumulation.  

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Observed the single basin sink across from triple sink to have a leak taking place at the drain line. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all plumbing  is in good repair. Ensure plumbing is repaired by a licensed plumber to prevent future leaking. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the walk in freezer unit to be leaking and have an accumulation of ice around the unit. Discussed with PIC. Ensure walk in freezer unit is repaired to prevent drip from occurring.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the seal on the floor in front of fryers to be degraded and accumulating food debris.  Discussed with PIC. Ensure flooring is smooth, non absorbent, and easily cleanable. Ensure flooring is repaired and being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food accumulation. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed the hood system light to not be in operation. Discussed with PIC. Ensure repairs are made so the light is able to be turned on and is up to the manufacturers recommended output of light. 

6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed multiple drain flies to be present near the back mop sink area. Discussed with PIC. Orkin was present during spot check, ensure facility has pest control treatment for drain flies before the follow-up date. A follow-up will take place on 6/25/24 to ensure pest eradication has taken place.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

Two containers of food contact equipment under the tables at the far back of the kitchen are observed soiled. Items in the containers include lids, pan grates and bun shoots. It appears that multiple events of food prep have dropped food debris into the container and several items seem to be in the early stages of decomposing (gooey/ slimy). This poses a risk to any foods that later come into contact with the items. The items and containers were all cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The floor under the shelves in the walk in freezer are observed in need of sweeping/ mopping. Previous conversations in relation to this situation were recalled by the inspector and PIC during the inspection. PIC is instructed to ensure that the facility floors are maintained clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. Education took place in relation to proper hand washing procedures and PIC is instructed to review with staff.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Numerous flies (of varying types) are observed in the vicinity of the drain behind the three part sink. Flies were observed both in flight as well as landed on the counter and containers along the north facing wall. On request of the PIC, inspector discussed using an enigmatic cleaner in the drains to help eliminate the breeding locations for drain flies. Using fly strips under counter was also discussed. Fly strips should only be used in areas where contamination of food contact items will not be a concern. Inspector instructed PIC to consult professional pest control. Inspector will follow up for compliance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing. 

Shelves in the walk in cooler are observed with an accumulation of mold forming. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to prevent the accumulation of contaminants in the facility.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: 5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. The hand sink in the drive through area is observed with the waste pipe leaking. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to repair and maintain in good working condition.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. An employee was observed to not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after washing their hands. PIC is instructed to review hand washing procedures with all employees to ensure correct technique.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  1) The area around the mop sink is observed with a black substance around the rim as well as along the bottom section of the pipe over the sink. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to maintain clean. 2) The shelves over the 3 part sink on the left side are observed with a brown substance that has begun to accumulate drips. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to maintain clean.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(O) (Pf) Food Employees and Conditional Employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as relate to disease that are transmissible through food as specified under 2-201.11 (A).

PIC only had approximately half of the current employees reporting agreements at the time of the inspection. Follow up will take place on 2/7/2020.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.13 (C) The floors under the shelves in the walk in freezer were observed in need of cleaning. Inspector suggested changing the cleaning frequency to a period shorter than once a month.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11 (C) A paper bag with foods intended for employee consumption was observed on a counter used for food preparation. The bag was moved during the inspection to the area designated for employee foods during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text: 2-201.11(A) (P) Facility had not yet completed the reporting agreements for their employees and had not yet started tracking any potential food born illnesses. Procedures were discussed with the PIC and copies of the forms distributed by Sangamon County Public Health were given during the inspection. Most employees filled out the reporting agreement during the inspection. Inspector will follow up on the 11th for compliance with the code.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 (Pf) A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. 

The PIC during the inspection could not find the written policy documenting the procedures in the facility for the clean up of vomit or diarrhea in the facility. Inspector will follow in ten days to verify the procedures used in the facility.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12 (E) (C) During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food dispensing utensils shall be stored in a clean protected location. Particulates were observed floating in water in the bottom of the ice scoop holder in the drive through window with the ice scoop stored in the container. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to clean often enough so as to prevent possible contamination of the in use utensil. The scoop and the container were cleaned during the inspection.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above).

Observed the prep cooler on the sandwich line to have multiple items at 50-51 degrees F (probed). Items included turkey, corned beef and mozzarella cheese. The items had all been in the cooler since approximately 9 a.m. this morning (5 hours). The situation was discussed with the PIC and the items were discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-130 Ready to eat food shall be stored in a matter to prevent cross-contamination.

In the ice machine, a black substance (believed to be mold by the inspector) was observed along the edges of the deflection shield as well as on the food side of the door. Discussed proper cleaning procedures (wash/rinse/sanitize) with the PIC and instructed them to clean often enough so as to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

Observed the sanitizer in the 3 part sink to be at approximately 50 parts per million (ppm) Quat sanitizer. Quat sanitizers should be at a minimum of 150 ppm to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces. Discussed with the PIC and the compartment was changed during the inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

Observed the sanitizer bucket bellow the meat slicer to be at 0 ppm sanitizer. Discussed with the PIC and the bucket was changed during the inspection.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

Observed a pair of tongs used for handling of desserts to be stored in contact with a counter. Inspector discussed with the person in charge (PIC) the possible avenues of contamination this could pose to a ready to eat (RTE) food. The tongs were placed in cup during the inspection.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

On arrival, the sanitizer compartment in the 3 part sink was registering 0 parts per million (ppm) of Quat sanitizer. 
Quat based sanitizers are required to be 150-400 ppm to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces. It was discovered that the bag attached to the machine had run out. The bag was replaced and the resulting solution registered 150 ppm Quat.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. 

Observed the sani bucket to be registering 50-100 ppm Quat. Quat sanitizers must be between 150 to 400 ppm to effectively sanitize surfaces. Discussed with the PIC and the bucket was reset during the inspection.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

Observed 1) the floor in the walk in cooler to be soiled with food debris and frost. 2) the floor in the walk in cooler to be soiled with general debris. 3) the floor under shelves in the drive though area to have sauce packages and other items. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to ensure the floors are cleaned well enough so as to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

Observed the condenser in the walk in freezer to have a thick accumulation of frost and ice cycle coming off of it. Discussed the issue with the PIC and directed to ensure food safe from cross contamination.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

Observed a coat laying in the racks reserved for food syrups and other food implements. When pointed out to management the coat was moved to the area reserved for employee belongings.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-130 Ready to eat food shall be stored in a matter to prevent cross-contamination.

Observed an accumulation of black mold to bb growing on the tray in the ice machine. Showed to the PIC and instructed to clean at regular intervals.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750-160bGloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

Observed an employee wearing gloves to handle food, adjust the dial and press buttons on a machine and then move directly back to handling food. Inspector discussed with the employee that they should change gloves when moving between tasks that could potentially contaminate their gloves. Employee changed gloves.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

Observed a serving of chicken fingers and a drink set off to the side and stored on the ice machine in the back. When going to show the PIC food had been removed but the drink remained. Discussed with the PIC and directed to educate employees.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

During the inspection, sanitizer in the three part sink was tested to be at 100 p.p.m. Quat sanitizers should be 150 to 400 p.p.m. Sanitizer is produced at the correct concentration through a machine (verified from a bucket sanitizer located in a different part of the facility). While discussing with PIC, they suggested that the sink could have had water added that diluted the concentration.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
750-860 The food-contact surfaces of fixed equipment shall also be  protected from contamination.

Observed water in the bottom of the ice scoops holder for the large ice machine in the back. Particulates could be seen floating in the water that was making contact with the ice scoop. Discussed with the PIC who said that it was emptied weekly. Suggested emptying it more often and cleaning at each emptying interval.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

Observed a cart located in front of the sink in the rear of the facility. Cart was later moved to make access to the sink possible.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

Observed the vent over the sandwich prep area to be soiled with accumulate dust. Instructed PIC to clean regularly to prevent build up.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control. Observed drain flies in the food handling/prep area.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors. Observed minor food detritus under work stations, suggesting sweeping more often.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: 750-240 Observed a plastic container holding two bags of thawing cooked veggies in the fourth sink. No water was observed running over the thawing peppers. The food was pulled from the sink and returned ot the walk-in cooler.  Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed the ice scoop holder to have about two inches of water and debris in the base. Bucket was detached from the side of the ice machine and moved through wash, rinse, and sanitizing. Discussed the daily monitoring of the ice storage location.   Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed two portion cups being used as scoops in the mint bit storage container by the drive-thru window. Cease use of portion cups and provide a scoop with a proper handle that can extend from the food. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-280 A straining ladle is observed stored handle down into a container on the preparation cooler. Ladle is removed for washing every four hours so storage location is up to Arby's, however, make sure that the handle is presented out to employees. Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed an employee switch tasks from emptying garbage cans to taking order and collecting cash and finally grabbing foods. Discussed handwashing between tasks - especially between handling garbage or money and then foods or food equipment.  Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-830a Observed dish operator move some equipment through washing and rinsing cycles but not the sanitizing step. Items were placed on-top of air drying equipment in the fourth sink. Discussed sanitizing purpose and contact time. Dishes were pulled and moved through all cycles properly. Even non-food contact surfaces (such as ice scoop bucket and food trays) should be sanitized. All equipment and utensils placed in dish washing facilities shall be exposed to all dish washing cycles.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750-830f Observed old date marking stickers intact on washed equipment. Day dots and other labels should be removed prior to or as part of the washing process. Make sure that day dots are removed from equipment prior to restocking. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dish washing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dish washing machine operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the cabinets beneath the soda service station to be soiled with garbage and syrup spills. Clean the cabinets. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 Observed a leak at the faucet of the four compartment sink. Manager stated that the faucet has been addressed twice and does not currently have an outstanding work order. When  water is completely shut-off for the evening the leaking ceases. See that the plumbing is repaired.  All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 The floor underneath the ice cream machine on the drive-thru line is observed with water and liquid debris running from underneath this machine to the floor drain in the center of the table beverage station. Clean the floor paying attention to a possible water leak causing the ponding water on the floor. See that the floor drain is cleaned while floor cleaning is conducted. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 The plumbing beneath the four-part sink is observed soiled from waste water. Clean the plumbing. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1300 There is a rack for storage of chemical spray bottles located on the back wall of the cookline behind a microwave and over wrapped buns. This presents two problems: 1) chemicals are being stored over food and food equipment; and 2) the spray bottles are located high and just about an arms reach away from standing position. The roll rack of buns was pulled away from beneath the buns to correct the violation. Manager stated he can move the spray rack to an adjacent wall: making the bottles more accessible and no longer a spill potential.  Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda nozzles in the lobby drink station to be soiled. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the soda nozzles at the lobby drink station.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed food debris in the bottom reach-in freezer. Clean the bottom reach-in freezer.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed a cutting knife stored in between dressings in the prep cooler. Food contact surfaces and clean utensils should be stored in a manner to prevent cross contamination.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed cups that came in on a truck last night stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Cups were moved at least 6" off the ground during the inspection.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink to have a slow drain. Repair the hand sink.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed a box of food stored on the floor in the walk in cooler. All food must be stored at least 6" off the floor.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee eating food in the kitchen. Employees must eat in designated dining areas.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed some frost accumulation in the walk in cooler right outside the walk in freezer. All surfaces must be smooth and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda nozzles in the drive thru area to be soiled with a small amount of mold accumulation. Clean the food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the shelves where prepped food is stored in the walk in cooler to be soiled. Clean the shelves. 2). Observed the top of the knife holder near the four compartment sink soiled with food debris. Clean the knife holder. 3). Observed the bottom of the reach-in freezer to have food debris. Clean the bottom of the reach-in freezer. 4). Observed the display cooler to be soiled with food splash. Clean the display cooler.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the faucet near the deli slice machine. Repair the leak at the faucet near the deli slice machine.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor drain underneath the prep sink to be soiled. Clean the floor drain.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed a mop stored improperly. Mops must be inverted or hung to dry.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed no certified FSSMC manager at the beginning of the inspection. A certified food manager was present near the end of the inspection. For high risk restaurants, a FSSMC is required for all food shifts.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed tomatoes and other food items stored on the floor of the walk in cooler/ walk in freezer. Food must be stored at least 6" off the floor. Properly store the food.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.
